Connect with Sudarshan in[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sudharshanchary/)


#### **Key Takeaways**


- Hospitality technology is becoming more action-oriented, to meet the needs of an experiential business.
- AI and integrated hospitality platforms help organizations move from understanding guests to acting on that understanding in the moments when it matters most.


In[our previous post,](https://www.agilysys.com/en/blog/your-ai-advantage-pace-integration-not-features/) we explored why pace and integration are essential to unlocking AI’s value in hospitality. The next challenge is putting that intelligence to work where it matters most: during the guest experience.


For decades, hospitality technology has evolved from managing reservations and transactions to building increasingly rich guest profiles. Properties can recognize returning guests, remember preferences, track loyalty, and personalize offers with a level of insight that would have been difficult to imagine a generation ago. Yet despite this progress, a gap remains between what organizations know about their guests and what they can do with that knowledge while the guest is still on property.


#### **When Intelligence Arrives Too Late**


This is the natural limitation of business intelligence. While it has enabled hospitality providers to become very good at understanding guests before and after the stay, the next challenge is putting that intelligence to work while the guest is still there.


> ”
>
>
> A guest may arrive at a resort and be recognized immediately as a valued returning visitor. Their loyalty status and years of stay history are readily available. But once the stay begins, that data often becomes harder to apply consistently because information doesn’t travel with the guest across the property.


Guests who felt known at check-in can feel anonymous by dinner. Problems that could have been resolved while the guest is still on property become service recovery efforts days later. The organization understands the guest, but the operation often struggles to act on that understanding in real-time.


#### **The Challenge of Operationalizing Intelligence**


The next phase of hospitality technology is making existing intelligence available when employees can act on it. Consider how the industry approaches revenue opportunities. Upselling has traditionally been one of hospitality’s easier challenges to solve because it occurs at a clearly defined point in the guest journey. When a guest checks in, there is a natural opportunity to offer a room upgrade or a premium package.


Cross-selling during the stay, however, is more difficult because opportunities emerge throughout the guest journey and depend on changing circumstances. Consider a guest whose golf plans are disrupted by weather. In many operations, that simply results in a cancelled tee time. Yet the property may already have data that shows the same guest frequently books spa treatments, participates in wellness activities, or has demonstrated other similar preferences during previous stays. A different opportunity exists, but recognizing it requires the operation to connect information that traditionally lives in separate places.


The same principle applies to service recovery. A disappointing spa experience becomes valuable intelligence the moment it occurs, but it only matters if it drives timely action. If the feedback is reviewed after the guest departs, the opportunity is gone. If it is surfaced while the guest is still on property, the experience can be recovered before the relationship is damaged. In both scenarios, success depends on acting while the guest is still on property.


#### **The Power of an Ecosystem: Moving From Systems of Record to Systems of Action**


Operationalizing intelligence requires a connected ecosystem where information moves effortlessly across the entire guest journey: from front desk to retail to spa to golf, and even to their guest room. Instead of remaining inside reports or individual applications, guest context becomes part of the workflows that happen where hospitality is delivered.


> ”
>
>
> As intelligence becomes more accessible across the operation, systems begin to evolve beyond simply recording activity. They help organizations respond to situations as they develop, recover issues before they escalate, identify opportunities before they disappear, and maintain awareness of the guest throughout the stay. In other words, they evolve from systems of record into systems of action.


AI’s value comes from helping organizations act on guest intelligence faster and more consistently. By connecting information from across the operation and surfacing relevant context at the moment it is needed, AI can reduce the distance between knowing and acting.


#### **A More Responsive Future**


Hospitality has long understood what exceptional service looks like. The industry’s best operators have spent decades creating memorable experiences through anticipation, recognition, personalization, and thoughtful service recovery. Delivering that level of service consistently across every interaction, however, remains difficult.


> ”
>
>
> When awareness can move with the guest from one interaction to the next, service becomes more connected. Problems can be addressed sooner. Opportunities can be identified while they still exist. Recognition can extend beyond check-in and become part of the entire stay. The result is a more responsive guest experience that allows employees to deliver more personal attention at scale.


The future of hospitality will be shaped by how effectively organizations apply guest intelligence during the stay. When insight becomes part of everyday operations, employees are better equipped to create the experiences guests remember most.
